title: VPC Defensive Patterns & Evidence Automation for Private Deploys
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for private deployment network hardening focused on three coordinated pieces: (1) VPC defensive patterns (segmentation + firewall rules), (2) strong mTLS and certificate lifecycle, and (3) audit/evidence automation and SIEM export mapping for compliance bundles.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: eng-private-deployments, eng-sre, security, solutions-engineering.
- Scope: Redwood Private (VPC-connected deployments + on-prem variants). This doc targets customers and internal SREs implementing hardened network posture and automated evidence collection for audits (SOC2 / ISO-like requests).

High-level principles (TL;DR):
- Default-deny: explicit allow rules only; assume east-west is untrusted unless explicitly permitted.
- Least-privilege for network flows and RBAC for control-plane operations (RBAC v2).
- mTLS everywhere for service-to-service within the private footprint; terminate only in trusted sidecars or ingress proxies.
- Centralize audit collection; export normalized events to SIEM with deterministic schema to ease queries and evidence bundles.
- Automate evidence collection and signing; store time-bound bundles in customer audit bucket (immutable + retention metadata).

1) VPC defensive patterns (reference topologies)
ASCII diagram (core pattern - minimal):

  Customer Edge / Transit VPC  <--- peering/interconnect --->  Private Deployment VPC
  +----------------------+                                      +----------------------+
  |  Shared services      |                                      |  Infra VPC           |
  |  NAT, Transit GW      |                                      |  - Bastion (restricted)|
  +----------------------+                                      |  - App subnets (private)|
                                                                  |  - DB subnets (private) |
                                                                  |  - Egress GW / Proxy    |
                                                                  +----------------------+

Notes: separate subnets by trust level: management (bastion, runbooks), control plane, app, data-plane (DB), telemetry. Use route table isolation + subnet-level ACLs where supported.

Recommended security group / firewall layering (AWS / GCP patterns):
- Per-service security groups narrowly scoped to source SGs and ports. Avoid CIDR-based allow lists except for service egress proxies.
- Network ACLs (stateless) to set coarse-grain deny for known-bad ports and block wide ranges; use SGs for application level.
- Central egress proxy (TLS intercept is not recommended unless contractually allowed) - instead require services to only talk outbound to approved destinations via proxy with allowlist.
- Management plane (bastion) restricted to customer ACLs / SSO-based ephemeral access, MFA, and jump-host audit.

Firewall example snippets (short):
- AWS Security Group (high-level):
  - Name: sg-app-service
  - Ingress: Allow TCP 443 from sg-ingress-proxy (security-group id)
  - Ingress: Allow TCP 9000 from sg-control-plane
  - Egress: Allow 443 to sg-egress-proxy

- GCP firewall rule (conceptual):
  - direction: INGRESS
  - priority: 1000
  - action: allow
  - sourceTags: [ingress-proxy]
  - allowed: tcp:443

- Example iptables snippet for hardened host (notes for on-prem):
  iptables -P INPUT DROP
  iptables -A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
  iptables -A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT
  iptables -A INPUT -p tcp -m multiport --dports 22,443,9000 -s 10.0.0.0/16 -j ACCEPT
  # reject noisy ports
  iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 23 -j REJECT

2) mTLS pattern and certificate lifecycle
Goal: mutual authentication for all internal RPCs and HTTP endpoints. Key elements: identity, rotation, revocation, and auditability.

Minimal requirements:
- All service-to-service connections must present a valid client cert signed by the organization CA (short-lived leaf certs preferred, TTL 6–24h depending on environment).
- Use SPIFFE-like identities (spiffe://redwood/env/role/service) in SAN to map to RBAC subject.
- Sidecar model: envoy/istio-like sidecars terminate mTLS locally; app receives plaintext on localhost only. Alternative: library TLS for tiny footprint, but sidecar preferred for uniform policies.
- Cipher suites: prefer TLS1.3 only; restrict to AEAD suites (e.g., TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256). Disable RSA key transport.
- OCSP / revocation: maintain revocation list in control plane; sidecars fetch revocation/CRL at short intervals or consult central authz service.

Certificate rotation and bootstrap (recommended flow):
- Bootstrap: host uses ephemeral bootstrap token (short TTL) obtained via instance identity (cloud metadata + OIDC) to request leaf cert from private CA via mTLS-protected endpoint.
- Rotate: renew at 50% of TTL, automated via sidecar or cert agent; log rotation event to audit stream with prev_fingerprint and new_fingerprint.
- Emergency revoke: control plane marks certificate id in revocation store, triggers immediate rejects by sidecars (poll / push mechanism).

Practical config checklist for teams:
- [ ] Enable TLS 1.3 only in ingress/egress proxies and sidecars
- [ ] Use SPIFFE identity format and map to RBAC v2 subjects
- [ ] Implement automated rotation agent (certbot-like) in each node/sidecar
- [ ] Store private CA root in KMS/HSM when available; limit root access to secops

3) RBAC v2 (control plane + network-aware attributes)
Redwood RBAC v2 goals: role-based rules with attributes that can reference network identity (spiffe ID, source IP ranges, certificate fingerprint). Keep policies machine-readable for export.

Example RBAC v2 policy (YAML snippet, conceptual):
  - apiVersion: rbac.redwood/v2
    kind: Policy
    metadata:
      name: admin-operator
    subjects:
      - kind: ServiceAccount
        id: spiffe://redwood/prod/ops/manager
    resources:
      - kind: deployment
        name: '*'
    verbs: [read, write, deploy]
    conditions:
      - type: NetworkRange
        value: 10.5.0.0/16
      - type: CertificateFingerprint
        value: 'sha256:AB12...'

Design notes:
- Policies must be versioned and stored in a git-backed policy repo; use signed commits for production rollouts.
- Policy evaluation logs must include request_id, principal_spiffe, matched_policy_id, decision, and rationale for evidence.

4) Audit log schema (normalized)
We export a deterministic JSON schema from the control-plane and network proxies so SIEM ingest is straightforward. All logs must be in UTC (ISO-8601).

Audit event schema (fields):
- event_id: string (uuid)
- timestamp: string (ISO-8601 UTC)
- source: string (control-plane | sidecar | ingress-proxy | bastion)
- request_id: string (trace/req id)
- principal: string (spiffe id or user id)
- action: string (http:POST /deployments; auth:token-exchange; network:connection)
- resource_type: string (deployment|certificate|firewall-rule|db)
- resource_id: string
- decision: string (allow|deny|error)
- decision_reason: string (policy-match id or firewall rule id)
- outcome_status: string (200|403|...)
- src_ip: string
- dst_ip: string
- src_cert_fingerprint: string|null
- dst_cert_fingerprint: string|null
- raw_request: string (truncated, base64 if binary)
- labels: list of strings (optional tags)

Example event (single line JSON):
{"event_id":"b3a4-...","timestamp":"2024-11-03T21:03:12Z","source":"sidecar","request_id":"r-19b2","principal":"spiffe://redwood/prod/api/my-service","action":"http:POST /v1/predict","resource_type":"endpoint","resource_id":"/v1/predict","decision":"allow","decision_reason":"policy-123","outcome_status":"200","src_ip":"10.5.2.14","dst_ip":"10.5.3.2","src_cert_fingerprint":"sha256:...","dst_cert_fingerprint":"sha256:...","raw_request":"eyJ...","labels":["canary"]} 

Retention and signing for evidence bundles:
- Evidence bundle must include: control-plane audit slice (time-range), sidecar logs (same window), firewall rule snapshot (current), RBAC policy snapshot (git commit hash), mTLS cert inventory (fingerprints + expiry), and system config (k8s manifests or VM images).
- Bundle must be signed with org key (GPG or AWS KMS sign) and checksum stored in immutable store (S3 with Object Lock or GCS retention).

Automation runbook (one-button):
1) Orchestrator triggers: generate bundle for time-window T (defaults: last 30 days or custom range).
2) Collect: pull logs from centralized logging (e.g., aggregator) with query by timestamp and request_id prefix.
3) Snapshot: call infra tooling to export firewall rules (aws ec2 describe-security-groups / gcloud compute firewall-rules list), RBAC repo commit hash, CA inventory via PKI service.
4) Package: tar.gz the artifacts, sign, and push to secure audit bucket with metadata.json (range, created_by, git-refs).
5) Post: send notification to customer / compliance channel and create retention ticket.

Automation pseudo commands (example):
  # collect audits
  ./audit-tool collect --start 2024-10-01T00:00Z --end 2024-10-31T23:59Z --out ./bundle-202410.tar.gz
  ./audit-tool sign --in bundle-202410.tar.gz --kms-key arn:aws:kms:...
  aws s3 cp bundle-202410.tar.gz s3://redwood-audit-bucket/customer-123/ --acl private --metadata created_by=Aisha

5) SIEM export mappings (examples)
- Splunk HEC: post each audit event into HEC with index=audit, sourcetype=redwood:audit, and include event_id as _id. Use HEC batching and verify idempotency by request_id.
- Elasticsearch / OpenSearch: ingest pipeline should parse timestamp, event_id, principal, action, decision, and create a keyword field for resource_type to ease aggregations.
- Syslog: only used for legacy appliances; ensure JSON over TCP and tag with app=redwood-audit.

Filebeat minimal config snippet (for sidecar logs):
filebeat.inputs:
- type: log
  paths: ["/var/log/sidecar/audit.log"]
  json.keys_under_root: true
  json.add_error_key: true
output.elasticsearch:
  hosts: ["https://es-intake:9200"]
  index: "redwood-audit-%{+yyyy.MM.dd}"

6) Hardening checklist (operational runbook)
- Network / VPC
  - [ ] All subnets tagged by trust level and documented (owner: infra-eng)
  - [ ] Default security groups replaced with explicit-deny baseline (owner: eng-sre)
  - [ ] External ingress only via controlled ingress proxy (owner: solutions-eng)
  - [ ] Egress allowlist enforced through egress proxy (owner: infra)

- mTLS & PKI
  - [ ] All services present valid SPIFFE certs (owner: eng-runtime)
  - [ ] Automatic rotation enabled (cert TTL <= 24h for prod) (owner: eng-runtime)
  - [ ] Root CA stored in KMS/HSM and rotated annually (owner: security)

- RBAC & Policy
  - [ ] Policies stored in git with signed commits and policy-id mapping (owner: eng-platform)
  - [ ] RBAC audit logs include policy_id and decision rationale (owner: eng-platform)

- Audit & Evidence
  - [ ] Evidence automation run weekly and on-demand (owner: compliance)
  - [ ] Bundles signed and immutable copy exists (owner: compliance)
  - [ ] SIEM retention configured per compliance requirements (owner: secops)

- Monitoring & SIEM
  - [ ] Alerts for certificate expiry < 48h (owner: secops)
  - [ ] Alerts for repeated TLS handshake failures from specific IP ranges (owner: eng-sre)
  - [ ] Dashboard: policy-denials by principal and by resource (owner: product-analytics)

7) Troubleshooting notes & operational runes (informal)
- If sidecars report revocation but traffic still allowed: check sidecar CRL refresh interval and ensure control-plane pushed revocation marker.
- If SIEM shows gaps: confirm filebeat/forwarder checkpoint and ensure agent hasn't rotated logs without checkpointing.
- For customer-managed VPNs, ensure MTU mismatch doesn't break TLS handshakes; recommended MTU 1436 for IPSEC over cloud.

8) Open questions / TODOs
- TODO: define exact TTL recommendations per environment (staging vs prod) — propose prod=12h, staging=24h (open for review).
- TODO: integration with customer KMS for root CA signing (legal / compliance gating).
- Q: Do customers want CA logs in evidence bundle or just cert inventory? (ask compliance on next sync).

9) References and quick links
- Confluence: /infra/vpc-patterns (linked above)
- Internal PRs: infra PR#812 - vpc segmentation automation
- Slack threads: #private-deploys (search "mTLS rotation incidents")

Notes to self: this doc is a working draft — iterate with secops and solutions-eng before marking final. Keep examples minimal and point to policy repo for canonical YAML.

Appendix A — sample small RBAC policy library (policy ids):
- policy-001: infra-view-only
- policy-123: app-deployers
- policy-999: compliance-audit-reader

Appendix B — minimal evidence metadata.json example:
{
  "bundle_id": "bundle-202410",
  "start": "2024-10-01T00:00:00Z",
  "end": "2024-10-31T23:59:59Z",
  "created_by": "Aisha Banerjee",
  "signed_by": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:key/abc",
  "artifacts": ["audit/control-plane.jsonl","audit/sidecars.tar.gz","infra/firewall_snapshot.json","policy/git-ref:abcd1234","pki/cert-inventory.json"]
}

End of playbook (draft).
